source.title: SafeSeek: Universal Attribution of Safety Circuits in Language Models
source.authors: Miao Yu; Siyuan Fu; Moayad Aloqaily; Zhenhong Zhou; Safa Otoum; Xing fan; Kun Wang; Yufei Guo; Qingsong Wen

record.file_problem: No file problem; the full paper is present, though some tables are flattened.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests safety localization by identifying sparse circuits and measuring safety after circuit ablation, and tests safety erosion during helpfulness fine-tuning. These are conceptually related tests, not the original studies’ methods.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test harmful-example fine-tuning, per-token KL concentration, compliant-prefix or suffix attacks, decoding changes, or why safety would be shallow. It reports circuit ablations and helpfulness-fine-tuning outcomes. Fine-tuning outcomes cited from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: Two of the study's own results bear on claim versions. (1) Circuit ablation and isolation localize safety refusal in sparse head and neuron subsets of LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen-3-8B; removal raises jailbreak ASR to about 82–99% (V5). (2) A LoRA helpfulness fine-tuning baseline on HelpSteer2 lowers the AdvBench harmless rate (V2). These use different methods from the original sources. The study is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that both backdoor behaviour and safety alignment are governed by highly sparse circuits orthogonal to general-utility components, found via STE-based mask optimization. They also conclude that tuning based on these circuits (SaCirT) removes backdoors efficiently and preserves safety during helpfulness fine-tuning, mitigating the 'alignment tax'.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses gradient-optimized binary circuit masks and circuit ablation, rather than fine-tuning on harmful or benign examples to measure safety loss or per-token KL analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper varies circuit granularity and reports differing safety and utility outcomes; helpfulness-fine-tuning results also differ between LoRA and SafeSeek circuit tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: Backdoors implanted by fine-tuning (refusal, jailbreak and mislabel triggers) are localized in sparse circuits. Ablating these circuits removes the backdoor; Cbkd alone reproduces it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning-implanted trigger behaviours are localized in a sparse, utility-orthogonal subnetwork.

fits_no_version.finding: Restricting helpfulness fine-tuning to (or away from) the safety circuit keeps the AdvBench harmless rate near baseline (94.0 / 93.8 vs 95.0 / 94.5; Qwen 99.2 vs 100.0).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Circuit-restricted fine-tuning mitigates benign-fine-tuning safety erosion.

record.problems: The reported ASR outcomes have no uncertainty estimates stated. Some table entries are flattened, and the helpfulness-fine-tuning values in Section 5.4 differ from the appendix values. The study tests circuit localization rather than the claim's specific weight/rank formulation.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible results were left out.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples. The backdoor injection trains on trigger-based poisoned data and is not measured as general harmful compliance.
Only one benign dataset (HelpSteer2) and one recipe (LoRA, 16 epochs). No variation in dataset size and no carefully chosen benign data.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
No individual-weight or LoRA-rank localization; weight and layer granularities were bypassed. No test of whether the circuit is what harmful fine-tuning alters.
No training to deepen safety. SaCirT preserves safety during benign tuning but is not a depth intervention.

missing.what: Qwen-3-8B Gunsafe ASR after circuit removal: ID 0.3→99.2, OOD 6.3→94.2. Also Qwen MMLU 77.1→74.9 and HellaSwag 53.9→52.5.
Qwen-3-8B Csafe isolated-circuit ASR: ID 2.3%, OOD 7.8% (vs base 0.3 / 6.3).
LLaMA alignment granularity ablation: neuron-only (0.32%) ASR 96.1 / 96.6; head-only (8.89%) 60.2 / 60.0; without STE 21.1 / 12.5; with utility costs.
Utility of LLaMA Gunsafe: GSM8k 67.6, MMLU 64.2, HellaSwag 52.9 (base 72.5 / 69.7 / 54.7).

record.verdict_notes: Internal inconsistencies: the abstract (3.03% heads, 0.79% neurons) and Table 2 Csafe (0.32% heads, 1.38% neurons) describe different masks. Section 5.4 and Appendix D.2 give different base and fine-tuned harmless rates. Section 5.1 names SafeEdit but the results report AdvBench. SaCirT is described as both updating only the circuit and excluding the circuit. ASR is judged by Llama-Guard-3-8B, with no uncertainty on ASR results. Preprint.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not fine-tune on harmful examples to measure harmful-request compliance.
The study tests helpfulness fine-tuning on HelpSteer2, not a range of ordinary or carefully selected benign datasets or dataset sizes.
No per-token KL divergence comparison between aligned and base models is reported.
No compliant opening, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change intervention is tested.
The study tests sparse head/neuron circuits, not whether particular weights or low-rank adaptation ranks carry safety.
The study does not investigate what causes safety to be shallow.
The study does not train safety to operate beyond the first response tokens or test whether such training holds up.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Helpfulness fine-tuning with the LoRA baseline
rows.note: The paper reports a decrease in harmless rate after helpfulness fine-tuning; this indicates some erosion, not near-total loss of safety.
rows.check: Row is correct (95.0→89.3, about a 6-point drop). Two problems with the source: Section 5.1 says harmlessness is measured on SafeEdit, but the results report AdvBench; and there is no uncertainty. It duplicates r3, which gives different numbers for the same experiment.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Helpfulness fine-tuning with SafeSeek circuit tuning
rows.note: The reported rate changes little under circuit tuning, which the authors contrast with the LoRA baseline.
rows.check: SaCirT is the study's own mitigation method compared with the LoRA baseline. It shows how well the method preserves safety, not whether benign fine-tuning erodes safety, so it should not be linked to V2. The paper also describes it inconsistently: the abstract says the circuit is 'excluded', while Section 4.4 says only circuit parameters are updated.
